elements.text: A method of unlocking a hand-held electronic device, the device including a touch-sensitive display, the method comprising:
detecting a contact with the touch-sensitive display at a first predefined location corresponding to an unlock image;

continuously moving the unlock image on the touch-sensitive display in accordance with movement of the contact while continuous contact with the touch screen is maintained, wherein the unlock image is a graphical, interactive user-interface object with which a user interacts in order to unlock the device; and

unlocking the hand-held electronic device if the moving the unlock image on the touch-sensitive display results in movement of the unlock image from the first predefined location to a predefined unlock region on the touch-sensitive display.

elements.quote: As soon as you power it up, you’re presented with a software button with an arrow on it that sits at the bottom of the screen in a channel with the message ‘Slide to Unlock’ that animates to suggest that you slide the button to the right.
elements.evidence_summary: The review describes a graphical arrow button in a channel that users slide right, but does not explicitly describe uninterrupted contact or continuous tracking of the image with the finger. An iOS 7 review separately reports movement of a whole screen layer rather than a small slider, so the earlier mechanism is not established across the full iOS 1–9 range.

basis.reasoning: MacStories describes a software arrow button in a channel and direct finger manipulation of screen elements, supporting the graphical interactive-object portion. It does not explicitly describe uninterrupted contact or continuous image tracking. AppleInsider directly reports that iOS 7 moves an entire screen layer instead of the small slider, supporting the version caveat; no publication date was shown for the quoted MacStories page.
